potential_errors: Section 7.1's final total-variation generalization is underspecified if read as requiring only marginal time-law calibration. strengths: Theorem 3.3 correctly distinguishes dense approximation from exact realization. Lemma 3.2 places positive-rate semigroup data inside the full phase-correlation body even without strict conditional negative definiteness; convex interior containment then permits actual finite energy atoms. The real dimension kd(d−1) gives the stated support bound.

Theorem 4.1 constructs one positive joint phase law, not separate incompatible pair marginals. Its additive Poisson kernels have disjoint Fourier supports, giving every integer moment of every pair difference simultaneously. The positivity criterion and spectral-width bound 2π/Δ follow directly.

Lemma 2.1 legitimately extends the witnesses to arbitrary Hermitian ensembles: conditional spectral sampling reproduces all off-diagonal transfer entries with one joint energy law. Neither population preservation nor finite energy moments is silently required.

The circular cut representation, small-spacing asymptotic and uniform Fourier tail establish the completeness claim in Theorem 5.3. Choosing Δ first and then K avoids an unjustified interchange of limits. The converse is supported by an explicit Cauchy construction, so the private predecessor is not an unproved dependency.

The four-phase measurement cancels unwanted transfer terms even for population-mixing channels. The coefficient sampling and Hoeffding normalization give exp[−Ng²/(8A²)]. The supplied rational verifier uses valid Machin and Taylor/geometric-tail bounds for both numerical designs; numerical LP interpolation is not presented as an exact certificate.

The clock results are mutually consistent. Corollary 7.1 concerns fixed uncertain menu entries; Theorem 7.3 changes the resource to fresh continuous time sampling. Its translation-TV estimate is frequency-independent, and Corollary 7.4 correctly derives the inverse-timing-error lower bound on alias spectral width.
strong_novelty_candidates: Exact finite-support static aliases for all interior phase-correlation tuples at rationally independent times, with the positive-rate real semigroup application and consequent indistinguishability under adaptive channel queries.
An explicit bounded-energy joint ensemble matching all pair coherences on an entire sufficiently coarse uniform grid, through the additive Poisson-kernel construction.

Complete finite odd-harmonic certificates for every physical real rate matrix outside the cut cone, valid against arbitrary static Hermitian ensembles and implementable with bounded single-shot observations.

The combined clock-resource picture: dense exact-alias fragility, spectral-width timing budgets, a bounded-time randomized repair without an energy prior, and a quantitative inverse-error energy cost for nearby aliases.
summary: This version gives a coherent sampling-dependent identifiability theory for real dephasing semigroups: exact finite-support aliases at rationally independent times, bounded-energy aliases on coarse grids, and complete finite odd-harmonic separation outside the cut cone. The central proofs survive static checking, including the interiority step, reduction from arbitrary Hermitian ensembles, and normalization of shot and timing budgets. The randomized-clock repair is valid under its continuous-sampling and independence assumptions, not for arbitrary jitter or digital rounding. I find no unresolved objection invalidating a main theorem. Minor revision should qualify the final total-variation generalization and describe the shot counts strictly as sufficient. This assessment uses the supplied PDF extraction and source; I did not execute code, browse references, recompute the PDF hash, or verify context isolation.
weaknesses: The finite-menu theorem is an existence result rather than an efficient synthesis method. Its support bound provides no energy upper bound or conditioning guarantee. The inverse-error lower bound is useful but does not determine optimal bandwidth or construction complexity.

The energy-prior-free repair requires a genuinely continuous, calibrated time law independent of the hidden Hamiltonian and measurement phases. A finitely supported clock distribution has TV distance one from the ideal uniform law; bounded rounding error alone therefore cannot justify the repair. The manuscript acknowledges this substantial implementation limitation.

The coarse-grid positivity condition, harmonic design and shot counts are sufficient rather than optimal. General dimension-dependent experimental costs and comparisons with sharper estimators are not developed.

The experimental guarantees assume ideal preparations, readout observables and setting probabilities, with a specified reference rate matrix. State-preparation/readout errors and uncertainty in the rates receive no quantitative budget. Together with the fresh single-use restriction, this limits immediate laboratory applicability without invalidating the stated model.
